entry.title: SEC obtains $5.4M default judgment against NanoBit Limited for operating a fake cryptocurrency trading platform (pig-butchering / relationship-investment scam)

category.term: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York

entry.content:
On June 25, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York entered a final judgment by default against NanoBit Limited and co-defendants in SEC v. NanoBit Limited et al. (No. 1:24-cv-09413, filed December 11, 2024). According to the SEC's complaint, NanoBit operated a fraudulent cryptocurrency trading platform to which victims were recruited through social media and dating apps; defendants cultivated fake personal relationships with investors before inducing them to deposit funds on the NanoBit platform. NanoBit created fictitious account balances, manipulated price feeds, blocked withdrawal requests, and demanded tax payments on phantom profits. The final default judgment orders disgorgement, prejudgment interest, and civil monetary penalties totaling approximately $5.4 million. Law360 identified the action as the first SEC crypto pig-butchering case resolved by default judgment. The SEC published the order as Litigation Release No. LR-26576 on June 29, 2026.
Primary source: SEC Litigation Release No. LR-26576 (June 29, 2026; primary source retrieved) — https://www.sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/litigation-releases/lr-26576
Relevant to: crypto exchanges, digital-asset trading platforms, fintech platforms with crypto products, AML and fraud compliance teams

entry.title: CFTC has ongoing investigation into Polymarket over deceptive marketing; bipartisan senators Curtis and Schiff send letter to CFTC Chairman Selig demanding disclosure of scope of probe

category.term: CFTC (investigation) / U.S. Senate — Senators John Curtis (R-UT) and Adam Schiff (D-CA)

entry.content:
As reported by the Wall Street Journal, CNBC, Forbes, and the New York Times on June 26, 2026, the CFTC has an ongoing investigation into Polymarket, the largest U.S.-based prediction market by trading volume. The investigation had not been previously publicly disclosed; the prior CFTC and DOJ investigation into Polymarket was dropped in July 2025. The CFTC declined to comment; Polymarket declined to respond. The reported probe follows a Wall Street Journal investigation documenting that Polymarket paid social-media content creators to post videos of staged winning outcomes, with Journal analysis of 1,100 videos identifying a systematic deceptive-marketing campaign. On June 26, 2026, Senators John Curtis (R-UT) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) sent a bipartisan letter to CFTC Chairman Michael Selig requesting disclosure of the scope and status of the investigation and whether the deceptive-marketing conduct violates CFTC rules or federal law; the senators wrote: 'The public-facing behavior alleged here does not resemble a sober financial market designed for hedging or price discovery.' A consumer advocacy group also filed suit against Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan and CMO Matthew Modabber alleging deceptive advertising targeting college students.

entry.title: Michigan AG secures state-court TRO temporarily halting Kalshi internet sports wagers; 14-day order through July 13 with geolocation mandate and $120,000/day non-compliance fine

category.term: Michigan Department of Attorney General (Dana Nessel) / Ingham County Circuit Court

entry.content:
On June 29, 2026, Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel announced she secured a temporary restraining order in the Ingham County Circuit Court (Case No. 26-1087-CZ, Hon. Rosemarie Aquilina) halting KalshiEx, LLC from offering or advertising its internet sports betting operation to Michigan residents while the state's lawsuit continues. The state-court order follows a June 25 ruling by the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Michigan granting the Attorney General's motion to remand the case to state court after Kalshi had removed it. The underlying lawsuit, filed in March 2026, alleges Kalshi offered unlicensed online sports betting under the guise of trading event contracts in violation of Michigan's Lawful Sports Betting Act, without licensing from the Michigan Gaming Control Board. As reported by The Detroit News and CBS News Detroit, the order runs 14 days through July 13, 2026, requires Kalshi to use a Michigan Gaming Control Board-licensed third-party geolocation provider to block users located in Michigan, and imposes a $120,000-per-day fine for non-compliance; Kalshi, which maintains it is subject to exclusive federal jurisdiction, said it would fight the decision.
Primary source: Michigan Dept. of Attorney General press release (June 29, 2026; primary source retrieved; links the court's TRO order, Case No. 26-1087-CZ); order terms corroborated by The Detroit News and CBS News Detroit (June 29, 2026) — https://www.michigan.gov/ag/news/press-releases/2026/06/29/ag-nessel-secures-order-temporarily-halting-unlawful-kalshi-michigan-operations

entry.title: ICBA launches six-figure DC ad campaign against CLARITY Act stablecoin yield; passage odds fall to 42–50%

category.term: Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA)

entry.content:
As reported by The Guardian (June 28, 2026), the Independent Community Bankers of America — representing approximately 4,000 community banks — launched a six-figure advertising campaign in Washington D.C. opposing provisions in the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act, H.R. 3633) that would allow stablecoin issuers to pay yield or rewards on holdings. ICBA argues the provisions could draw $1.3 trillion in deposits away from community banks and imperil $850 billion in loans to small businesses and farmers. Galaxy Research has reduced its estimate of the bill's passage probability to approximately 50%, down from ~60% earlier in June; prediction market Polymarket prices passage at approximately 42%, down from highs near 73%. A unified updated draft of the bill is expected to be released during the July 4 weekend, per multiple reports. The Senate Banking Committee passed the bill on May 14, 2026 (15-9); the bill requires approximately seven Democratic votes for the 60-vote cloture threshold. The Senate is scheduled to break July 4 and resume July 13, with approximately four active session weeks remaining before August recess.
Coverage: The Guardian (June 28, 2026; as reported by — secondary source; corroborated by Blockhead.co, StartupFortune, Bitcoin Magazine, Bitget/CryptoRank, June 28-29) — https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/jun/28/crypto-v-community-local-lenders-fight-stablecoins-law

entry.title: Senate Democrats ask Appropriations Committee to bar CFTC from funding state prediction market preemption suits

category.term: U.S. Senate (17 Democrats)

entry.content:
On June 26, 2026, seventeen Democratic senators — led by Senators Blumenthal (D-CT), Merkley (D-OR), Schiff (D-CA), and Padilla (D-CA), joined by Senators Cantwell, Cortez Masto, Durbin, Heinrich, Hickenlooper, Hirono, Lujan, Murphy, Rosen, Schatz, Smith, Warren, and Whitehouse — sent a letter to the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government requesting that the Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bill prohibit the Commodity Futures Trading Commission from using federal funds to prevent states and Tribes from enforcing their gambling laws and gaming compacts against online prediction markets. The letter identifies eight states already sued by the CFTC (Connecticut, Illinois, Arizona, Wisconsin, New York, Minnesota, Rhode Island, and New Mexico) and states: 'Through engaging in this campaign of litigation and intimidation, the CFTC risks becoming an instrument and enabler of online prediction markets' efforts to bypass states' consumer protections and oversight, creating a race-to-the-bottom in gambling.'
Primary source: Sen. Schiff Press Release — schiff.senate.gov (June 26, 2026; primary source retrieved) — https://www.schiff.senate.gov/news/press-releases/news-sens-schiff-padilla-join-blumenthal-merkley-in-push-to-end-cftc-assault-on-state-prediction-markets-oversight/

entry.title: CFTC proposes formal data-reporting rules for event contracts, ending eight-plus years of no-action relief (NPRM 9261-26)
entry.content:
On June 25, 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (Press Release 9261-26) proposing amendments to Parts 15, 16, and 17 of CFTC regulations to establish an alternate data-reporting framework for fully collateralized event contracts. The proposal would require reporting markets, futures commission merchants (FCMs), clearing members, and foreign brokers to report event contracts under Parts 15-18 of the CFTC's regulations rather than under Parts 38, 39, 43, and 45, replacing an informal reporting regime that has operated under staff no-action letters since 2017. A public comment period is open; the comment deadline will be set in the Federal Register notice.
Primary source: CFTC Press Release 9261-26 (June 25, 2026) — https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9261-26
Relevant to: prediction-market platforms, FCMs, clearing members, foreign brokers dealing in event contracts

entry.title: Kalshi files federal lawsuit against Illinois over SB3019's 15% sports prediction market gross receipts tax and state licensing requirement for DCMs; TRO and PI sought ahead of July 1 effective date

category.term: KalshiEx LLC (plaintiff) v. Governor JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, Illinois Gaming Board — U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois

entry.content:
Kalshi filed a 31-page federal complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois on June 23, 2026, naming Governor JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, and five Illinois Gaming Board officials as defendants. SB3019 imposes: (a) a 15% gross-receipts tax on sports prediction market revenues; (b) a state licensing requirement for CFTC-registered designated contract markets (DCMs). Both provisions take effect July 1, 2026. Kalshi argues both provisions are preempted by the Commodity Exchange Act's exclusive-jurisdiction clause (7 U.S.C. § 2(a)(1)(A)). The complaint seeks a temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction, and permanent injunction.

entry.title: W.D. Michigan denies Robinhood preliminary injunction — sports event contracts are NOT swaps; CEA does not clearly preempt state gambling law

category.term: U.S. District Court, W.D. Michigan (Judge Paul Maloney)

entry.content:
On June 18, 2026, U.S. District Judge Paul Maloney denied Robinhood's motion for a preliminary injunction against Michigan state gambling enforcement. The court held: (1) sports event contracts are not 'swaps' under the Commodity Exchange Act; and (2) even if they were swaps, it is not clearly established that the CEA would preempt Michigan's state gambling law.
